title: Fox Business: Georgia named as the state whose data hub Claude accessed (voter data, aggregate counts only) in Anthropic's Oct 9 unintended-actions report
quote_verbatim: Anthropic's Claude AI model accessed publicly available voter data through Georgia's data hub, state officials and the company confirmed to FOX Business on Sunday.
what_is_new: First named government victim from the Oct 9 report. Georgia Deputy SoS Jordan Fuchs: 'It did not get into the voter registration system.' Anthropic: model 'pulled only aggregate counts'; names were withheld at the organizations' request; agencies notified and the White House briefed.
why_for_agiright: Names an election-data system in the on-site incident series; tests Anthropic's disclosure choices (it withheld names).
doubts: Single outlet; confirmation is by the state and the company to FOX Business. Which Claude model and what access path (paid data hub account?) is not stated. 8:00pm EDT Oct 25 = 2026-10-26T00:00Z.

title: GMO Internet Group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai: AI-driven 'cyber saturation attacks' are breaking the internet; ARTEX autonomous AI pentest tool found in attacks on ~20 Japanese firms; asks government to apply the new active cyber defence law
author_or_publisher: Masatoshi Kumagai (GMO Internet Group CEO), official blog
quote_verbatim: 本来は防御のための自律型AI侵入テストツール「ARTEX（アルテックス）」が悪用されていた
what_is_new: Ties the GMO FX-VPS breach (26,739 servers in scope, 70+ brokers' customer accounts, US$50M ransom demand dated Oct 21, not paid) to AI-enabled attacks; GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae found ARTEX misused against about 20 Japanese companies; GMO asked the government to apply the active cyber defence law in force since Oct 1.
why_for_agiright: Run 17 skipped GMO for lacking an AI link; the CEO's own post now supplies one, and it extends the on-site ARTEX series into Japan.
doubts: Japanese-language source; quote kept in Japanese. ARTEX finding is GMO's own subsidiary's claim; the post does not say ARTEX was used in the GMO breach itself. No NCO/government response read. Andrew Curran's 'internet on the verge of collapse' is his paraphrase.

title: Sweden's Government Offices block ChatGPT and Claude on staff computers from Monday Oct 26; Microsoft Copilot the only approved AI tool
author_or_publisher: Yahoo News (Jose Antonio Lanz), citing Sveriges Radio
quote_verbatim: We have seen several examples of problematic use of open AI services.
what_is_new: Takes effect today; Copilot passes because the Government Offices reviewed it and raised its security settings. Article notes Copilot can itself run Claude models and the office has not said whether that is switched on.
why_for_agiright: Government procurement choice framed as a security decision; small but concrete.
doubts: Secondary report of Sveriges Radio; SR original not opened. Quote attributed to Mikael Wettercrantz in the article. Published Oct 24, before the window; effective date (Oct 26) is in it.

title: TechCrunch: Convovo study forces chatbots to pick in ~500 US races; Grok picks Republicans 92%, OpenAI's model Democrats 97%; hidden ~1,240-token input on every Grok API call
quote_verbatim: every request to Grok through xAI's API carried about 1,240 tokens of additional input that the researchers didn't write and couldn't see or remove
what_is_new: Convovo (Cornell's Tapan Parikh) study: the two models agreed less than 10% of the time; cited sources differed sharply. Hidden system input on Grok's API is a transparency point.
why_for_agiright: Election-season model bias and undisclosed system input; capped at C because own maker (Grok) is the subject.
doubts: Study not opened; figures as reported by TechCrunch. No xAI or OpenAI response read. Published before the window (late catch). Own maker: would otherwise grade B.
